A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PoSh and DOCENT research and contain 26 complete pages, including Appendix A.1–A.4. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection establish that all substantive content matches; only the publication header and arXiv stamp differ.

before.justification: v2 reports original human-annotation results, metric evaluations on DOCENT and CapArena, reinforcement-learning comparisons, and component evaluations in Tables 2–9 and Figure 9.

after.justification: v3 retains the original annotation, benchmark, reinforcement-learning, and component-evaluation results in Tables 2–9 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The scene-graph extraction, identifier construction, question-answering verification, and score aggregation procedures are identical in Section 3 and Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DOCENT artwork and CapArena web-image coverage, including the same complex-scene subset and DOCENT reward-training task. No dataset, population, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2, 3, and 6, including the embedding baselines, DSG, DCScore, LLaVa Critic, and GPT4o/GPT5 settings. The SFT comparison in Table 7 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix A.2–A.4 retain identical annotation procedures, sample sizes, evaluation metrics, thresholds, model configurations, and SFT/DAPO training settings.

E4.justification: The complex-scene CapArena analysis, student-versus-expert annotation comparison, and scene-graph extraction and verification analyses are unchanged, including Figure 8 and Tables 8–9.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same significance reporting at alpha = 0.05, annotator-agreement measures, and additional-annotation counts. No seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting changes occur.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 2 retains PoSh mistake/omission F1 scores of 0.580/0.680, and Table 7 retains the overall-quality preference score of 0.135. Appendix results and Figure 9 are also identical.

T1.justification: The scene-graph definitions and granular/coarse scoring equations in Section 3 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about PoSh, DOCENT, human alignment, image-type robustness, reward-function effectiveness, and detailed artwork description.

C2.justification: Interpretations of robustness, the reinforcement-learning mistake/omission tradeoff, annotation differences, and component errors are unchanged. The limitations and accessibility qualifications in Sections 9–10 are also retained verbatim.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, prompts, pseudocode, hyperparameters, API access dates, H100/CUDA details, runtime reporting, and code/data access statements are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and Appendix A.1.1 comparison with Davidsonian Scene Graph remain identical. Research positioning and novelty claims do not change.

P1.justification: v3 adds 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' to every page and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All body wording, titles, author information, section ordering, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added running publication header and updated first-page margin stamp make limited visual changes. Rendered page bodies otherwise match exactly, including all figures, tables, captions, placement, and pagination.

improvement.justification: v3 changes only the publication header and arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and appendices are identical, so these administrative edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
